Nasdaq Financial Data Analysis

A Python analysis of Accrued Expenses Turnover across companies and countries from 2010 to 2015 using Nasdaq Data Link.

View GitHub ↗Open in Google Colab ↗
Executive overviewBusiness / analytical problemObjectiveApproachMethodologyKey insightsResults / conclusionsTechnical notes

Executive overview

This project uses the Nasdaq Data Link API to analyse Accrued Expenses Turnover and compare how the metric varies across companies, years and countries between 2010 and 2015.

Business / analytical problem

Financial ratios can vary materially across companies and markets. The analysis needed a clean workflow for retrieving API data, selecting the relevant observations and making cross-company and cross-country differences understandable.

Objective

Retrieve, clean and explore the metric, then use descriptive statistics and visualisations to identify differences in level and trend.

Approach

JSON responses from the API were converted into a Pandas DataFrame, cleaned and filtered to the target metric. The analysis then compared company trends and country-level averages.

Methodology

Python, Requests and Pandas were used for data retrieval and transformation, while Matplotlib was used for visualisation.

Key insights

The analysed values were widely dispersed. The dataset mean was about 26.91 versus a median of about 13.75, indicating that relatively high observations influenced the average. In the analysed 2010–2015 sample, the Bahamas had the highest country average, followed by the United States and the United Kingdom.

Results / conclusions

The notebook provides a reproducible path from API retrieval to financial-metric comparison, with clear descriptive outputs and visual summaries.

Technical notes

Running the notebook requires a Nasdaq Data Link API key configured as NASDAQ_API_KEY in Google Colab Secrets. The key is not stored in the repository.
